# Command The Coordinators of the primary stations come together to form the [color=#1b67a5]Command[/color] of the Lark Region, the closest form of authority that the Lark has. They usually have access to special equipment and their own rooms, and are often targets by those who seek to plunge the region into a state of havoc.
## Personnel [color=#1b67a5]Command[/color] is made up of the heads of each department, being the [color=#c96dbf]Lodge Supervisor[/color], the [color=#5b97bc]Medical Director of Kemak[/color], the [color=#f39f27]Mercenary Coordinator[/color], and above all else, the [color=#1b67a5]Sector Coordinator[/color].
## Taking Charge Congratulations on your ascension to authority! Hopefully people want you here, and your new [color=#a4885c]responsibilities[/color] include keeping personnel and equipment safe as well as keeping watch for any possible invasions.
Don't forget, you still have a job! Your fancy tools don't earn you a day off, you still have to fill in for any staffing shortages, helping out struggling workers and teaching the newcomers.
You might get away with just sitting around and letting people do things for you, but it's wiser to get active and work alongside them. Remember to move your workers around to have them do what they like doing or what they do best.
## Your Locker
To deal with your new soul-crushing tasks, every head is given special items to lead the disarrayed populous. Most of your new shiny tools can be found in your [color=#a4885c]locker[/color].
Your [color=#a4885c]remote[/color] is very simple but profoundly underestimated. A small but mighty force, your remote can open and close [color=#a4885c]airlocks[/color], spin the [color=#a4885c]bolts[/color] to lock them, or toggle [color=#a4885c]emergency access[/color]. It can do this from a distance.
The remote influences where people move around. Heads can lock personnel out of dangerous areas or let people in to grab something really quickly.
You also have access to your very own [color=#1b67a5]Command[/color] channel, like every other department. However, yours is particularly special as the people who can hear you have [color=#a4885c]entire departments[/color] at their fingertips. Use this to communicate with other heads and be a representative of what your workers want or need.
The [color=#1b67a5]Sector Coordinator[/color] gains access to the lucrative [color=#a4885c]master encryption key[/color], letting them tune into every radio channel from the Relay. This is extremely valuable, allowing you to remotely coordinate between departments and crews. [color=#a4885c]Don't waste this vital advantage![/color]
To make the swamp of paperwork (that will definitely overwhelm you) even harder to deal with, you have generously been given a [color=#a4885c]stamp[/color] in your locker. Use this to sign paperwork. After you stamp it, it typically can't be changed. Look it over first.
